newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW-Ekran subscription rate low.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Ekran subscription rate low.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments on an announcement by Ekran Bhd that its rights issue was undersubscribed by 62.77 percent.
JASON CHONG, ANALYST WITH SMITH ZAIN SECURITIES

"As far as the share price is concerned there will be a massive share overhang problem over the next two years. Based on my calculations I see a share overhang of 32 million shares or 26 percent of Ekran's share capital.
"I don't expect the share price to perform for the next two years."
AZLIN ALIAS, ANALYST AT CASPIAN SECURITIES:
My first thoughts were that they are clearing up the share overhang issue. The market was expecting it will go to the underwriters, who will subsequently sell it to the market.
Now what we are seeing is the shares are taken up by (Ekran executive chairman) Ting Phek Khiing, therefore there will not be any share overhang.
Though the Securities Commission says he will have to divest, the impact will not be as the market expected.
This is an indication of Ting taking responsibility, the risks, to show that he has full backing (of the government).
There are rumours of him selling Granite (Industries Bhd), PWE (Industries Bhd) and Pac Chem (Pacific Chemicals Bhd to Ekran to get cash.
So all three companies under him personally will then be under Ekran.
(Ting is currently the controlling shareholder of the three companies).
The market has already expected the rights to be undersubscribed. This news will alleviate worries for the underwriters.
EKRAN ANALYST AT PHILEOALLIED SECURITIES:

"It (the news) wasn't surprising. The next question is where would he (Ting) get the money from. I don't think it's logical for him to sell his other companies, especially when they have subcontracts for Bakun. Banks are one option.
"(A possibility is) a restructuring to pull all the other companies into Ekran. People are saying he needs the cash, and that's one way he could get the money.

"I think sentiment will be quite bad (on the stock) immediately after this. It might drop a little bit further, but probably won't see any drastic falls. We have a reduce rating, which we'll keep for the moment.
"I am more concerned about what is after Bakun, how will they (Ekran) sustain earnings beyond that. This round, they did a rights issue, but what will they do then?
"If they do another rights issue, the dilution effect will keep doubling.
LAI TAK HEONG, RESEARCH DIRECTOR AT SOCGEN-CROSBY
I suppose Tan Sri Ting must show confidence in the project by picking up the rest of it.

In some ways it was all underwritten. But what they wanted here was a strong commitment from the promoter -- to show that he believes this thing will happen and that two years later people will relook at it and rerate the project.
But it's a lot of funds to raise because there's a one-for-one rights issue for the Bakun project one year down the road.
It may affect other big cash calls down the year like Time Telecommunications (a unit of Time Engineering Bhd ), those with no immediate income flow type.
I would think it will have a slight dampening effect on the market.
Generally, people will worry that the next underwriting issue like Time Telekom, what will happen?
It does not augur well for other for other big cash calls.
As a whole, banking groups with big merchant banks involved in big cash calls will be affected.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
